To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

depression is related to low adherence to Highly Antiretrovial Therapy in HIV positive men in São Paulo regardless of age and gender, that men who have sex men are more prone than men who have sex women to develop depression, and that white or mixed race men have better adherence to treatment than blacks.
depression and non-adherence to antiretrovirals are related in men with HIV, and that the prevalence of depression is higher among black and mixed race MSM than among MSW.
the prevalence of depression was 25% in MSM, 15% in MSW and 20% in the total sample, while the prevalence of low adherence was 30% in MSM, MSW and in the total sample.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and psychological implications of depression and adherence in HIV-positive individuals.
the social and psychological implications of depression and adherence in men who have sex both with men and women.
the social and psychological implications of adherence to Highly Active Antiretroviral therapy in HIV-positive men.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability of developing depression is 4.17 higher for an individual showing non-adherent behavior to Highly Active Antiviral Therapy than for an individual showing adherent behavior.
adherence and depression are strongly related and that depression is a major barrier to adherence.

the prevalence of depression in MSM subjects is two times higher than in MSW subjects, and that the prevalence of low adherence to antiretoviral treatment is also two times higher among depressed patients than among non-depressed ones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adherence to antiretorviral treatment in depressed patients is a challenge for the health professionals.
adherence to Highly Active Anti-Retroviral Therapy and depression have an inverse and direct relationship, respectively.
depression and low adherence are related in the HIV population, and this relationship may be even more evident in black patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adherence to treatment should be a priority in order to reduce the risk of depression.
depression is a significant predictor of non-adherence and vice-versa.
depression is an important factor in adherence.
